turns.text: Ok so, tree problems. I always like to think about whether it's a DFS or a BFS shape of problem first, that's basically my starting point with anything tree-shaped, because the traversal order kind of falls out of that decision.

So essentially what we're doing here is going level by level, and each level is its own list in the output, which is basically a level order traversal, which is essentially BFS. Is the tree guaranteed to be binary?

Right, binary, so at most two children. I'm going to use a queue for this, which is the standard thing for BFS, and then essentially just collect the values as I go. So yeah, I'm ready to start coding.
Great, so that's all passing, which is basically what I expected because it's a pretty standard traversal at the end of the day. So yeah, I'm done, we can move on.
Complexity-wise it's O(n) because you're basically visiting every node one time, and the space is also O(n) essentially because of the queue.
